title: Commissioning workflow
summary: Commissioning brings a machine from installed hardware to verified operation in controlled steps: hardware check, I/O check, function test, process test and handover.

sections.heading: A proven sequence
sections.body:
1. **Visual and power check**: supplies, terminals, module positions.
2. **Hardware configuration**: download, compare configured and installed modules, clear diagnostics.
3. **I/O check (loop check)**: actuate every sensor and force every output (with the machine made safe), confirm each tag reacts on the right address.
4. **Analog check**: inject or simulate known values (for example 4, 12, 20 mA) and verify scaling.
5. **Function test**: run each sequence step by step, then automatically.
6. **Fault tests**: pull a sensor, open a stop circuit, simulate communication loss; the machine must react safely.
7. **Documentation and handover**.

sections.heading: Forcing with care
sections.body: Forcing overrides inputs or outputs regardless of the program. It is indispensable for loop checks and dangerous when forgotten: a forced output stays on even when the program says off. PLC Lab shows active forces in the toolbar and the CPU FORCE LED.
